BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p433/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p433/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p433/r1.claim: Al-Farra, Ibn al-Anbari, al-Tabrizi, and lexicons attest that sariy means a small river or stream; in Maryam it is one of several interpretations.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p433/r1.anchor: تفسير السرى بالنهر الصغير، والجدول هو المعروف من كلام العرب

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p433/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p433/r2.speaker: الحسن البصري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p433/r2.claim: Al-Hasan recited the verse and said Maryam’s child was a sariy; Khalid ibn Safwan clarified that Arabs call a stream sariy, and al-Hasan agreed.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p433/r2.anchor: فأسند عن الحسن - البصري، أبي سعيد - انه تلا الآية

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p433/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p433/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p433/r3.claim: The form is unique in the Quran; related forms occur in the night-travel verb, the Prophet’s Night Journey, and commands to Lot and Moses to travel by night.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p433/r3.anchor: ومعها من مادتها جاء فِعل السُّرى مضارعاً في آية الفجر

ITQAN:v2p566/r24.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p566/r24.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p566/r24.claim: سرى has plural سريان, like خصي and خصيان.

BURSEVI:v5p251/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p251/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p251/r3.claim: The voice came from below Mary, from a place lower than her beneath the hill; another account places it beneath the palm.
BURSEVI:v5p251/r3.anchor: من مكان أسفل منها تحت الأكمة

BURSEVI:v5p251/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p251/r4.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v5p251/r4.claim: On a reading with fatḥah on the mīm, the one beneath her is Jesus, calling to her after emerging from the womb.
BURSEVI:v5p251/r4.anchor: وفي "الأسئلة المقحمة" قرىء بفتح الميم يعني به عيسى لما خرج من البطن

BURSEVI:v5p251/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p251/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p251/r5.claim: The command not to grieve concerns Jesus’ birth and the dry place; grief is sorrow over lost benefit or present harm, and the particle is explanatory or a verbal noun with a suppressed preposition.
BURSEVI:v5p251/r5.anchor: أن مفسرة بمعنى أي : لا تحزني بولادة عيسى وبمكان القحط

BURSEVI:v5p251/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p251/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v5p251/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Gabriel struck the earth and a fresh-water spring flowed as a brook; sariyy is a small stream as the Prophet explained.
BURSEVI:v5p251/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن جبريل ضرب برجله الأرض فظهرت عين ماء عذب

BURSEVI:v5p251/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p251/r7.speaker: أرباب الحقيقة
BURSEVI:v5p251/r7.claim: Jesus announced prophethood in the cradle and, while still in the womb, sariyy signaled that he would be a lord and leader among people.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس؛ نوف
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Nawf identify the caller as Gabriel; ʿAlqama's reading substitutes ‘addressed her,’ which Abū Ḥayyān also takes to mean Gabriel.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r1.anchor: أي جبريل عليه السلام كما روي عن ابن عباس ونوف

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r2.claim: ‘From below her’ can mean a physically lower place; al-Ḥasan says Gabriel stood on a lower patch, perhaps out of reverence for Mary.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r2.anchor: وكان في بقعة من الأرض أخفض من البقعة التي كانت عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r3.claim: The claim that Gabriel stood beneath Mary to receive the child is improper because it attributes an unworthy act to the trusted angel of revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r3.anchor: والقول بأنه عليه السلام كان تحتها يقبل الولد مما لا ينبغي أن يقال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r4.speaker: أبو حيان؛ مجاهد؛ وهب؛ ابن جبير؛ ابن جرير؛ ابن زيد؛ الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers Jesus as the caller, with ‘below her’ referring to Mary: God made the newborn speak; this is reported from several early authorities.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r4.anchor: واستظهر أبو حيان كون المنادى عيسى عليه السلام والضمير لمريم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس؛ الحسن؛ الجبائي؛ مجاهد؛ وهب؛ ابن جبير؛ ابن جرير؛ ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r5.claim: The alternative caller-Jesus interpretation is transmitted from Mujāhid, Wahb, Ibn Jubayr, Ibn Jarīr, Ibn Zayd, al-Jubbāʾī, and, through al-Ṭabrisī, al-Ḥasan.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r5.anchor: وروي ذلك عن مجاهد ووهب وابن جبير وابن جرير وابن زيد والجبائي

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r6.speaker: قراء الابنان والأبوان وعاصم والجحدري وابن عباس والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r6.claim: These readers open the mīm of man, making it a relative pronoun and subject of ‘called’; it can mean either Jesus or Gabriel.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الابنان والأبوان وعاصم والجحدري وابن عباس والحسن في رواية عنهما ( من ) بفتح الميم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r7.claim: ‘Do not grieve’ can be parsed with explanatory anna or with an elided preposition before a verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r7.anchor: على أن أن مفسرة أو بأن لا تحزني على أنها مصدرية قد حذف عنها الجار

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r8.claim: Taking ‘beneath you’ as ‘under your command’ is possible but departs from the apparent meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r8.anchor: وقيل : تحت أمرك إن أمرت بالجري جري وإن أمرت بالإمساك أمسك وهو خلاف الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r9.speaker: البراء؛ الحاكم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r9.claim: Al-Ḥākim transmits from al-Barāʾ that sari means a stream and grades the report sound according to the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections; al-Bukhārī cites it suspended, while connected versions are mawqūf, not soundly raised to the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r9.anchor: أي جدولا كما أخرجه الحاكم في مستدركه عن البراء وقال : إنه صحيح على شرط الشيخين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r10.speaker: لبيد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r10.claim: Labīd's verse uses sari for a watercourse and is cited as lexical evidence for that meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r10.anchor: فتوسطا عرض السرى فصدعا مسجورة متجاوزا قلامها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r11.claim: A verse cited by Ibn ʿAbbās compares a generous person's bounty to a stream fed by rivers, illustrating sari as a channel.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r11.anchor: سهل الخليقة ما وجد ذو نائل مثل السرى تمده الأنهار

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r12.claim: One report identifies the stream as a channel from the Jordan that God caused to flow when Mary was thirsty.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r12.anchor: وكان ذلك على ما روي عن ابن عباس جدولا من الأردن أجراه الله تعالى منه لما أصابها العطش

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r13.claim: Other reports say Gabriel struck the ground and a fresh spring flowed, or Jesus caused it, as transmitted from Abū Jaʿfar; another view says it was already there and God pointed it out.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r13.anchor: وقيل : فعل ذلك عيسى عليه السلام وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r14.claim: The stream newly produced by a miracle best fits the passage's emphasis on extraordinary signs and its apparent wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r14.anchor: وما تقدم هو الموافق لمقام بيان ظهور الخوارق والمتبادر من النظم الكريم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r15.speaker: الحسن؛ ابن زيد؛ الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r15.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Zayd, and al-Jubbāʾī take sari to mean Jesus, a boy of exalted rank, deriving it from elevation rather than flowing water.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r15.anchor: وعن الحسن وابن زيد والجبائي أن المراد بالسري عيسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r16.claim: The Lord's provision explains why Mary need not grieve; calling God ‘your Lord’ and attaching the pronoun to her dignifies and reassures her.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p82#2/r16.anchor: والجملة تعليل لانتفاء الحزن المفهوم من النهي عنه والتعرض لعنوان الربوبية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r1.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read min taḥtihā with kasra on mīm and tāʾ: Gabriel called from below her, behind the hill where she stood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r1.anchor: {فناداها من تحتها} قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وحمزة والكسائي وحفص: {من تحتها} بكسر الميم والتاء، يعني جبريل عليه السلام، وكانت مريم على أكمة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r2.claim: The other readers use fatḥa on both letters, also identifying Gabriel, who called her from the slope of the mountain.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r2.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بفتح الميم والتاء، وأراد جبريل عليه السلام أيضا، ناداها من سفح الجبل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r3.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r3.claim: They say the caller was Jesus, who spoke as soon as he emerged from his mother's womb.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو عيسى لما خرج من بطن أمه ناداها: {ألا تحزني} وهو قول مجاهد والحسن (1)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r4.claim: The preferred view, held by Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Suddī, Qatādah, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and others, is that Gabriel heard her distress and called to her.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r4.anchor: والأول قول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما والسدي وقتادة والضحاك وجماعة: أن المنادي كان جبريل لما سمع كلامها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r5.anchor: {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} و"السري": النهر الصغير.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r6.claim: Another view takes under you to mean under your command: whatever she orders it to do, it does.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r6.anchor: وقيل: تحتك أي جعله الله تحت أمرك إن أمرتيه أن يجري جرى، وإن أمرتيه بالإمساك أمسك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r7.claim: Gabriel, or Jesus, struck the ground with his foot, bringing forth a spring of sweet water.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: ضرب جبريل عليه السلام -ويقال: ضرب عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام-برجله الأرض فظهرت عين ماء عذب وجرى (2)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r8.claim: Another account says God sent water through a dry river and revived the dried palm, which leafed, flowered, and ripened dates.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r8.anchor: وقيل: كان هناك نهر يابس أجرى الله سبحانه وتعالى فيه الماء وحييت النخلة اليابسة، فأورقت وأثمرت وأرطبت.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r9.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the sari is Jesus, a noble and elevated servant.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p226/r9.anchor: وقال الحسن: "تحتك سريا" يعني: عيسى وكان والله عبدا سريا، يعني: رفيعا (3)

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:24/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:24/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:24/r1.claim: The caller beneath Mary was Jesus; alternatively Gabriel, who was holding the child, or someone physically below her. Readers vary the case in “from beneath her,” parsed through the caller's pronoun or the palm's.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:24/r1.anchor: عيسى، وقيل جبريل كان يقبل الولد

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:24/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:24/r2.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:24/r2.claim: A report traced to the Prophet explains sarī as a stream; another interpretation takes it to mean Jesus, from sarw (nobility).

QASHANI:19:22-24/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:22-24/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:22-24/r4.claim: Gabriel called from below her heart's station, from nature, the source of her sorrow over pregnancy and possible disgrace.
QASHANI:19:22-24/r4.anchor: { فنادها من تحتها } أي: ناداها جبريل من الجهة السفلية بالنسبة إلى مقامها من القلب،

QASHANI:19:22-24/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:22-24/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:22-24/r5.claim: The stream beneath her is a current of rare natural science and knowledge of divine action-unity, granted as a sign of her selection.
QASHANI:19:22-24/r5.anchor: تحتك سريا } أي: جدولا من غرائب العلم الطبيعي وعلم توحيد الأفعال الذي خصك الله بها

QASHANI:19:22-24/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:22-24/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:22-24/r6.claim: The miraculous formation of the fetus from her semen alone is evidence of that divine gift.
QASHANI:19:22-24/r6.anchor: كما رأيت من تولد الجنين من نطفتك وحدها.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r6.claim: Jesus calls to Mary from beneath her and tells her not to grieve.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r6.anchor: { فناداها من تحتها } وهو عيسى عليه السلام { ألا تحزني

BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r9.claim: The sary beneath her is a stream of water in a land without flowing water, a sign that should comfort her.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p528/r9.anchor: جدولا من الماء جليلا آية لك تطيب نفسك

DURR-FULL:v5p494/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p494/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p494/r6.claim: A caller beneath Mary says not to grieve and says God placed a stream beneath her.
DURR-FULL:v5p494/r6.anchor: وناداها ملك من تحتها {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا}

DURR-FULL:v5p496/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p496/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p496/r7.claim: God made a channel from the Jordan for Mary; “sari” means a small stream.
DURR-FULL:v5p496/r7.anchor: فأجرى الله لها جدولا من الأردن فذلك قوله: {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} والسري الجدول

DURR-FULL:v5p501/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r9.speaker: علقمة
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r9.claim: Alqama reads that someone addressed Mary from beneath her.
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r9.anchor: عن علقمة أنه قرأ فخاطبها من تحتها

DURR-FULL:v5p501/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the caller as Gabriel and says Jesus did not speak until Mary brought him to her people.
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {فناداها من تحتها} قال: جبريل ولم يتكلم عيسى حتى أتت به قومها

DURR-FULL:v5p501/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r11.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r11.claim: Ikrima identifies the caller as Gabriel.
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r11.anchor: عن عكرمة قال الذي ناداها هو جبريل

DURR-FULL:v5p501/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r12.speaker: الضحاك وعمرو بن ميمون
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak and Amr ibn Maymun also identify the caller as Gabriel.
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r12.anchor: عن الضحاك وعمرو بن ميمون مثله

DURR-FULL:v5p501/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r13.speaker: البراء
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r13.claim: Al-Bara says the caller was an angel.
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r13.anchor: عن البراء {فناداها من تحتها} قال: ملك

DURR-FULL:v5p501/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r14.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r14.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says Gabriel called from below in the valley.
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r14.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {فناداها من تحتها} قال: جبريل من أسفل الوادي

DURR-FULL:v5p501/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r15.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r15.claim: Mujahid identifies the caller as Jesus.
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r15.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {فناداها من تحتها} قال: عيسى

DURR-FULL:v5p501/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r16.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r16.claim: Al-Hasan also says Jesus called Mary.
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r16.anchor: عن الحسن {فناداها من تحتها} قال: هو عيسى

DURR-FULL:v5p501/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r17.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r17.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b says the caller was the one Mary carried in her womb, who entered through her mouth.
DURR-FULL:v5p501/r17.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال الذي خاطبها: هو الذي حملته في جوفها

DURR-FULL:v5p502/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r1.speaker: زر بن حبيش
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r1.claim: Zirr ibn Hubaysh is reported reading “he called her from beneath her.”
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r1.anchor: عن زر بن حبيش أنه قرأ {فناداها من تحتها}

DURR-FULL:v5p502/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r2.claim: Qatada identifies the caller as the angel beneath the palm.
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r2.anchor: عن قتادة {فناداها من تحتها} أي الملك من تحت النخلة

DURR-FULL:v5p502/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r3.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r3.claim: Al-Hasan distinguishes readings: one identifies the caller as Gabriel, the other as Jesus.
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r3.anchor: عن الحسن قال: من قرأ من تحتها فهو جبريل ومن قرأ من تحتها فهو عيسى

DURR-FULL:v5p502/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r4.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r4.claim: Asim reads the phrase with accusative; that reading identifies Jesus, while genitive identifies Gabriel.
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r4.anchor: عن أبي بكر بن عياش قال: قرأ عاصم بن أبي النجود {فناداها من تحتها} بالنصب

DURR-FULL:v5p502/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r5.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the sari as a prophet, namely Jesus.
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r5.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله: {جعل ربك تحتك سريا} قال: نبيا وهو عيسى

DURR-FULL:v5p502/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r6.claim: Qatada says “sari” means a stream; Muhammad ibn Abbad responds it means a noble man in Arabic.
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r6.anchor: سمعت قتادة يقول: الجدول قال: فأخبر قتادة عني فإنما نزل القرآن بلغتنا إنه الرجل السري

DURR-FULL:v5p502/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says “sari” refers to Mary as noble, rejecting stream because the river would be beside, not under, her.
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r7.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله: {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} يريد نفسه أي سرى أسرى منه

DURR-FULL:v5p502/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r8.claim: A Prophetic report says the sari was a river God brought forth for Mary to drink.
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r8.anchor: عن ابن عمر: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: إن السري الذي قال الله لمريم: {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} نهر أخرجه الله لها

DURR-FULL:v5p502/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r9.claim: Another Prophetic report glosses the sari as a river.
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r9.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله: {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} قال: النهر

DURR-FULL:v5p502/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r10.speaker: البراء
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r10.claim: Al-Bara says the sari is a small stream or river.
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r10.anchor: عن البراء في قوله: {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} قال: هو الجدول وهو النهر الصغير

DURR-FULL:v5p502/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas calls it the river of Jesus.
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r11.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} قال: نهر عيسى

DURR-FULL:v5p502/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas also glosses “sari” as a stream.
DURR-FULL:v5p502/r12.anchor: عن عثمان بن محصن قال: سئل ابن عباس عن قوله: {سريا} قال: الجدول

DURR-FULL:v5p503/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r1.speaker: شاعر
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r1.claim: An unnamed poet uses “sari” for a watercourse as evidence for the stream interpretation.
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r1.anchor: قول الشاعر وهو يقول: سلم تر الدالي منه أزورا إذا يعج في السري هرهرا

DURR-FULL:v5p503/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas defines sari as a small river or stream and cites Arabic poetry as evidence.
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: إن نافع بن الأزرق قال له: أخبرني عن قوله عز وجل: {تحتك سريا} قال: السري النهر الصغير

DURR-FULL:v5p503/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r3.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak says the sari is a stream.
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله: {سريا} قال: الجدول

DURR-FULL:v5p503/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r4.speaker: عمرو بن ميمون وإبراهيم النخعي
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r4.claim: Amr ibn Maymun and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i give the same stream gloss.
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r4.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون وإبراهيم النخعي مثله

DURR-FULL:v5p503/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r5.claim: Al-Hasan first calls the sari noble; Hamid corrects him that it is a stream, and Hasan says rulers have taken Hamid from their gatherings.
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r5.anchor: عن قتادة أن الحسن تلا هذه الآية وإلى جنبه حميد بن عبد الرحمن الحميري {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا}

DURR-FULL:v5p503/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r7.claim: Mujahid says the word means river in Syriac.
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {سريا} قال: نهرا بالسريانية

DURR-FULL:v5p503/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r8.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the word means river in Coptic.
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {سريا} قال نهرا بالقبطية

DURR-FULL:v5p503/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r9.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r9.claim: Al-Hasan says the sari was Jesus; Khalid ibn Safwan notes Arabs call a stream sari, and Hasan accepts the correction.
DURR-FULL:v5p503/r9.anchor: عن سفيان بن حسين في قوله: {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} قال: تلاها الحسن فقال: كان والله

QUSHAYRI:v2p238/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p238/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p238/r7.claim: The voice from beneath Mary may have been Gabriel or Jesus; its purpose was to ease her loneliness and announce the noble child.
QUSHAYRI:v2p238/r7.anchor: أن المعني بقوله { من تحتها } : جبريل عليه السلام ، وقيل عيسى عليه السلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r1.claim: The one calling Mary is the baby she carried; the phrase من تحتها can mean from beneath her, or use من as a relative pronoun for the boy below her. The latter reading makes the newborn's speech a sign of Jesus and an honor to Mary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r1.anchor: ضمير الرفع المستتر في ( ناداها ) عائد إلى ما عاد عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r2.claim: Readers differ in parsing من تحتها: Nafi, Hamza, al-Kisai, Hafs, Abu Jafar, Khalaf, and Ruh read من as a preposition; Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Abu Bakr, and Ruways read it as a relative pronoun for the child.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r2.anchor: قرأ نافع ، وحمزة ، والكسائي ، وحفص ، وأبو جعفر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r3.claim: Specifying that the baby called from beneath her depicts him speaking as soon as he was born, before she lifted him, to comfort her at once and portray the intimate moment of birth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r3.anchor: ولإفادة أنه ناداها عند وضعه قبل أن ترفعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r4.claim: أنلا is explanatory of the call; the statement about the stream explains why Mary should not grieve, since her circumstances merit joy as a divine honor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r4.anchor: خبر مراد به التعليل لجملة { ألا تحزني }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r5.claim: سريا means a flowing stream; God provides pleasant food and drink as a visible honor and evidence of her innocence to Yusuf the carpenter and any witnesses. Water nearby and fresh dates out of season from a dead palm would be extraordinary; fresh fruit is more appealing than dried dates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p86/r5.anchor: السري : الجدول من الماء كالساقية ، كثير الماء الجاري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r1.claim: On the nominative reading of man, the caller is the newborn Jesus, as Mujahid, al-Hasan, Ibn Jubayr, and Ubayy say.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r1.anchor: قال أي ناداها المولود قاله مجاهد والحسن وابن جبير وأبي بن كعب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the caller as Gabriel; Alqama, al-Dahhak, and Qatada also hold this view.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r2.anchor: قال أي ناداها المولود قاله مجاهد والحسن وابن جبير وأبي بن كعب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r3.claim: The miraculous call is a sign of God's purpose; if Jesus called her, his speech clears her and removes suspicion, so she need not grieve.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r3.anchor: ففي هذا آية لها وأمارة أن هذا من الأمور الخارقة للعادة التي لله فيها مراد عظيم لا سيما والمنادي عيسى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r4.claim: The genitive reading of min marks a starting point; interpreters still differ whether the caller is Jesus or Gabriel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم والبراء بن عازب والضحاك وعمرو بن ميمون وأهل الكوفة وأهل المدينة وابن عباس أيضا والحسن «من تحتها»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r5.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r5.claim: A faction identifies the caller on the lower ground as Gabriel, Mary's earlier interlocutor; al-Hasan swore to this account.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r5.anchor: قالت فرقة: المراد جبريل المحاور لها قبل، قالوا: وكان في سعة من الأرض أخفض من البقعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r6.speaker: علقمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r6.claim: Alqama and Zirr ibn Hubaysh read “he addressed her from beneath.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r6.anchor: وقرأ علقمة وزر بن حبيش «فخاطبها من تحتها»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas's alternative wording specifies an angel calling Mary from beneath.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس «فناداها ملك من تحتها»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r8.claim: The particle an explains the call, with the sense “that is,” or “namely.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r8.anchor: وقوله ألا تحزني تفسير النداء ف «أن» مفسرة بمعنى أي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r9.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r9.claim: Al-Sari can mean a man of great qualities and standing; Qatada and Ibn Zayd interpret it this way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r9.anchor: و «السري» من الرجال العظيم الخصال السيد، و «السري» أيضا الجدول من الماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r10.claim: Most commentators take al-sari to mean the stream beside the palm trunk.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r10.anchor: وقال الجمهور أشار لها إلى الجدول الذي كان قرب جذع النخلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r11.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r11.claim: Al-Hasan first called Jesus a noble lord, then Ubayd ibn Abd al-Rahman corrected him that al-sari meant the stream; al-Hasan lamented that rulers had prevailed over him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11/r11.anchor: وروي أن الحسن فسر الآية فقال أجل لقد جعله الله سريا كريما، فقال عبيد بن عبد الرحمن الحميري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11#2/r1.claim: Shaking the dry trunk provides another sign: life and fruit can emerge from what is dead.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11#2/r1.anchor: ثم أمر بهز الجذع اليابس لترى آية أخرى في إحياء موات الجذع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11#2/r3.claim: The apparent account is that Jesus spoke to Mary and the palm trunk was dry; these signs comforted her.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p11#2/r3.anchor: والظاهر من الآية أن عيسى هو المكلم لها وأن الجذع كان يابسا وعلى هذا تكون آيات تسليها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r1.claim: They read min taḥtihā with fatḥa on both mīm and tāʾ; the other listed readers use kasra on both.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وابو بكر عن عاصم من تحتها بفتح الميم والتاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r2.claim: If the phrase is read with kasra, the caller may be the angel below the palm or below Maryam if she stood on a rise; it may instead be Jesus calling from the womb.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r2.anchor: فمن قرأ بكسر الميم ففيه وجهان أحدهما ناداها الملك من تحت النخلة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r3.claim: He says what the gaze looks upward toward is above and what it looks downward toward is beneath.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس كل مارفعت اليه طرفك فهو فوقك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r4.claim: He maintains that the angel addressed Maryam in either reading.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r4.anchor: وكان الفراء يقول ما خاطبها الا الملك على القراءتين جميعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r5.speaker: جمهور المفسرين واللغويين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r5.claim: Most exegetes and lexicographers take siriyyan as a small river; Abū Ṣāliḥ and Ibn Jurayj call it a stream, a Syriac loanword.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r5.anchor: أنه النهر الصغير قاله جمهور المفسرين واللغويون قال أبو صالح وابن جريج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r6.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r6.claim: They instead take siriyyan as Jesus, a noble man; Ibn al-Anbari says Hasan later returned to the river interpretation and notes that Arabs normally say rajulun sarī.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r6.anchor: انه عيسى كان سريا من الرجال قاله الحسن وعكرمة وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r7.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r7.claim: Maryam was distressed by the barren place, with no food, drink, or water for washing, so God reassured her by providing a stream and dates.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r7.anchor: حزت لجدب مكانها الذي ولدت فيه وعدم الطعام والشراب والماء الذي تتطهر به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r8.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r8.claim: Another explanation is that her grief came from giving birth without a husband; God sent a stream from Jordan and dates from the dry tree as a sign of His power to create Jesus.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p221#2/r8.anchor: أنها حزنت لما جرى عليها من ولادة ولد عن غير زوج فأجرى الله تعالى لها نهرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r1.claim: Some read min tahtiha as the person beneath Mary, while others read min as a preposition meaning from beneath her.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r1.anchor: قرأ بعضهم {من تحتها} بمعنى (1) الذي تحتها. وقرأ آخرون: {من تحتها} على أنه حرف جر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r2.claim: Al-Awfi's report and several others say Gabriel called from below the valley and Jesus did not speak until Mary brought him to her people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {فناداها من تحتها} جبريل، ولم يتكلم عيسى حتى أتت به قومها،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r3.claim: Mujahid says Jesus was the caller; Hasan via Qatada and one report from Saʿid ibn Jubayr agree, citing Mary's gesture toward him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {فناداها من تحتها} قال: عيسى ابن مريم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jarir select the view that the caller was Jesus.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224/r4.anchor: واختاره ابن زيد، وابن جرير في تفسيره (4)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r1.claim: The caller tells Mary not to grieve because God provided a sari beneath her; most authorities take sari as water or stream, which Ibn Jarir selects.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r1.anchor: {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} قال سفيان الثوري وشعبة، عن أبي إسحاق، عن البراء بن عازب:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says sari means a river; Amr ibn Maymun specifies a river from which she drinks.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: السري: النهر. وبه قال عمرو بن ميمون: نهر تشرب منه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says sari means river in Syriac; Saʿid ibn Jubayr says a small river in Nabataean, and al-Dahhak a small river in Syriac.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: هو النهر بالسريانية. وقال سعيد بن جبير: السري: النهر الصغير بالنبطية.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r4.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي وقتادة ووهب بن منبه والسدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r4.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi calls it a small river, Qatada a channel in Hijaz usage, Wahb a spring, and al-Suddi a river.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r4.anchor: وقال إبراهيم النخعي: هو النهر الصغير. وقال قتادة: هو الجدول بلغة أهل الحجاز.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r5.claim: Ibn Umar reports God produced a river for Mary; Ibn Kathir calls it very strange, and Ayub ibn Nahik is judged weak, munkar, and abandoned by hadith critics.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r5.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "إن السري الذي قال الله لمريم: {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} نهر أخرجه الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r6.speaker: الحسن والربيع بن أنس ومحمد بن عباد بن جعفر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r6.claim: Another view interprets sari as Jesus; Qatada and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd also transmit it, but Ibn Kathir prefers the river view because the palm follows.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p224#2/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: المراد بالسري: عيسى، عليه السلام، وبه قال الحسن، والربيع بن أنس، ومحمد بن عباد بن جعفر.

JISHUMI:v6p4538/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4538/r3.speaker: الحسن وشيبة ونافع ويحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v6p4538/r3.claim: These readers use kasra in من تحتها; the others use fatḥa. Either reading allows Gabriel or Jesus as the caller.
JISHUMI:v6p4538/r3.anchor: قرأ الحسن وشيبة ونافع ويحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم

JISHUMI:v6p4538/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4538/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
JISHUMI:v6p4538/r4.claim: On the kasra reading, Gabriel calls Mary from below the mountain.
JISHUMI:v6p4538/r4.anchor: قيل: هو جبريل ناداها من سفل الجبل

JISHUMI:v6p4538/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4538/r5.speaker: غير مسمى
JISHUMI:v6p4538/r5.claim: Another view says Jesus called from beneath Mary as he emerged.
JISHUMI:v6p4538/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو عيسى لما خرج من بطن أمه من تحتها

JISHUMI:v6p4544/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r18.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي والضحاك وقتادة
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r18.claim: Gabriel called to Mary from beneath her.
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r18.anchor: قيل: ناداها جبريل، عن ابن عباس، والسدي، والضحاك، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v6p4544/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r19.speaker: مجاهد ووهب وسعيد بن جبير وابن زيد وأبو علي والأصم
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r19.claim: Jesus called to Mary from beneath her.
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r19.anchor: وقيل: عيسى، عن مجاهد، ووهب، وسعيد بن جبير، وابن زيد

JISHUMI:v6p4544/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r20.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r20.claim: Sariy means a river; other views call it a small channel or stream.
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r20.anchor: قيل: نهرا، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير

JISHUMI:v6p4544/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r21.speaker: البراء بن عازب والأصم
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r21.claim: Sariy may mean a small channel.
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r21.anchor: وقيل: جدولا، عن البراء بن عازب، والأصم

JISHUMI:v6p4544/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r22.speaker: إبراهيم والضحاك وقتادة
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r22.claim: Sariy means a small river for Mary to drink from and wash after childbirth.
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r22.anchor: قيل: النهر الصغير، عن إبراهيم، والضحاك، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v6p4544/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r23.speaker: الحسن وابن زيد وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r23.claim: Sariy may mean Jesus, a noble and distinguished servant; al-Ḥasan swears he was such a servant.
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r23.anchor: وقيل: السري عيسى، عن الحسن، وابن زيد، وأبي علي

JISHUMI:v6p4544/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r24.speaker: غير مسمى
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r24.claim: Under you may mean the river runs beneath Mary's command, as in the verse about rivers running beneath; it may instead mean physically below her.
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r24.anchor: قيل: جعل النهر يجري تحت أمرها وتمسكه بأمرها

JISHUMI:v6p4544/r25.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r25.speaker: غير مسمى
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r25.claim: Gabriel struck the ground with his foot and a sweet spring appeared; another view credits Jesus' foot.
JISHUMI:v6p4544/r25.anchor: قيل: ضرب جبريل برجله فظهر ماء عذب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r1.claim: Min taḥtihā is explained as Gabriel, who acted like a midwife, or as Jesus; the latter is the reading of Asim and Abu Amr.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r1.anchor: {من تحتها } هو جبريل عليه السلام . قيل : كان يقبل كالقابلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r2.claim: Alternatively, min taḥtihā means below her position, as in the phrase about rivers flowing below; another account places the caller beneath a hill.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r2.anchor: وقيل : { تحتها } أسفل من مكانها ، كقوله : { تجرى من تحتها الانهار }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r3.claim: The readings reported from Nafi, Hamza, al-Kisaʾi, and Hafs keep min taḥtihā; the speaker in nādāhā may be the angel or Jesus.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r3.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحمزة والكسائي وحفص ( من تحتها )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r4.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r4.claim: Qatada says the pronoun in taḥtihā refers to the palm tree.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r4.anchor: وعن قتادة : الضمير في تحتها للنخلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r5.speaker: زر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r5.claim: Zirr and ʿAlqama read fa-khāṭabahā, “he addressed her from beneath.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r5.anchor: وقرأ زر وعلقمة : فخاطبها من تحتها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r6.claim: Asked about al-sariyy, the Prophet said it is a stream; Labid's poem uses the word for a stream.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r6.anchor: ( 658 ) سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن السري فقال : ( هو الجدول )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r7.claim: Alternatively, sariyy derives from sarw and refers to Jesus; al-Hasan says he was a noble servant.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r7.anchor: وقيل : هو من السرو . والمراد : عيسى وعن الحسن : كان والله عبدا سريا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r8.claim: The stream and dates console Maryam as miraculous signs of her purity and freedom from suspicion, showing her accusers that her virgin birth is part of extraordinary divine action.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p14/r8.anchor: لم تقع التسلية بهما من حيث أنهما طعام وشراب ، ولكن من حيث أنهما معجزتان

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r1.claim: One view identifies the caller from beneath Mary as Gabriel.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما : أن المنادي لها من تحتها جبريل , قاله ابن عباس , وقتادة , والضحاك , والسدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r2.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r2.claim: Another view identifies the caller from beneath her as her son Jesus.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنه عيسى ابنها , قاله الحسن , ومجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r3.claim: Min taḥtihā may mean from below Mary on the ground, with Mary above the caller.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما : من أسفل منها في الأرض وهي فوقه على رأسه ، قاله الكلبي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r4.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, min taḥtihā means from her womb, an explanation said to be in Coptic.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r4.anchor: الثاني : من بطنها : قاله بعض المتكلمين , بالقبطية .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r5.claim: Sariyyan may refer to Jesus as noble and high-ranking, from the expression for the noblest members of a people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r5.anchor: أن السري هو الرفيع الشريف مأخوذ من قولهم فلان من سروات قومه أي من أشرافهم , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وابن جبير وقتادة والضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r6.claim: Sariyyan may mean a stream, giving Mary water while the palm gives her food; on this view Gabriel is the caller.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r6.anchor: الثاني : أن السري هو النهر ، قاله ابن عباس ، ومجاهد ، وابن جبير ، وقتادة ، والضحاك ، لتكون النخلة لها طعاما , والنهر لها شرابا

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r7.claim: Sariyyan may be an Arabic word derived from sarā, to flow, as a poet's comparison to a stream fed by rivers shows.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r7.anchor: الثاني : أنه عربي مشتق من السراية فسمي السري لأنه يجري فيه ومنه قول الشاعر :

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r8.claim: The cited verse compares a generous man to a stream fed by rivers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p364#2/r8.anchor: سهل الخليقة ماجد ذو نائل مثل السري تمده الأنهار

FARRA:v2p164/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p164/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p164/r6.claim: In both readings of ‘she called from beneath,’ the caller is Gabriel; min taḥtihā means that he was below her.
FARRA:v2p164/r6.anchor: وقوله: فناداها من تحتها [24] و (ناداها من تحتها) وهو الملك في الوجهين جميعا.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p366/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p366/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p366/r1.claim: Sari can denote a river people cross by jumping.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p366/r1.anchor: وقيل : إن اسم السري يطلق على ما يعبره الناس من الأنهار وثبا

MUJAHID:v1p385#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p385#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p385#3/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the one calling from beneath Mary as Jesus son of Mary.
MUJAHID:v1p385#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ فناداها من تحتها ﴾ يعني عيسى بن مريم

MUJAHID:v1p385#3/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p385#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p385#3/r2.claim: Mujahid says sari means a small river in Syriac.
MUJAHID:v1p385#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله عز وجل ﴿ قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا ﴾ قال السري النهر الصغير بالسريانية

MUJAHID:v1p385#3/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p385#3/r3.speaker: البراء بن عازب
MUJAHID:v1p385#3/r3.claim: Al-Bara ibn Azib says sari is a stream, a small river.
MUJAHID:v1p385#3/r3.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب قال السري هو الجدول وهو النهر الصغير

MUQATIL:19:24-26/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:24-26/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:24-26/r1.claim: Gabriel called from below, on the ground while Mary stood above him on a rise, telling her not to grieve after she wished for death; sariy means a small stream.
MUQATIL:19:24-26/r1.anchor: فناداها } جبريل، عليه السلام، { من تحتهآ } ، يعني من أسفل منها في الأرض، وهي فوقه على رابية

MUQATIL:19:24-26/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:24-26/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:24-26/r2.claim: Sariy means a small river or stream.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r1.claim: The caller beneath Mary may be Gabriel, positioned lower than her, or Jesus speaking from beneath her skirt; in a reading reported for Medinan and most Kufic readers, the pronoun refers to the palm and the subject is implicit, either Jesus or Gabriel.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r1.anchor: أي الذي تحتها فمن فاعل وهو جبريل عليه السلام لأنه كان بمكان منخفض عنها أو عيسى عليه السلام لأنه خاطبها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r2.claim: The call comforts her about loneliness, food, drink, and what people will say; an here explains the words that follow.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r2.anchor: لا تهتمي بالوحدة وعدم الطعام والشراب ومقالة الناس وان بمعنى أي

NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r3.claim: Under you can mean nearby, or under your command, such that the stream obeys if ordered to flow or stop.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r3.anchor: قربك أو تحت أمرك إن أمرته أن يجري جرى وأن أمرته أن يقف وقف

NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r4.claim: Most commentators take sariyyan as a small stream; the Prophet explained it as a brook.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r4.anchor: نهرا صغيرا عند الجمهور وسئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن السرى فقال هو الجدول

NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r5.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r5.claim: Al-Hasan takes sariyyan to mean a noble master, namely Jesus.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r5.anchor: وعن الحسن سيدا كريما يعني عيسى عليه السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r6.speaker: خالد بن صفوان
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r6.claim: Khalid ibn Safwan told al-Hasan that Arabs call a brook sariyyan; al-Hasan agreed and returned to the stream interpretation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r6.anchor: وروى أن خالد بن صفوان قال له ان العرب تسمى الجدول سريا فقال الحسن صدقت ورجع إلى قوله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jesus or Gabriel struck the ground with his heel, bringing forth fresh water; the dry stream flowed, and the palm turned green, bore fruit, and ripened.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p34#3/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ضرب عيسى أو جبريل عليهما السلام بعقبه الأرض فظهرت عين ماء عذب

MAJAZ:v2p5/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p5/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p5/r1.claim: سريا means a stream or river; Labīd’s verse uses it for water.
MAJAZ:v2p5/r1.anchor: «سريا» (24) أي نهرا، قال لبيد بن ربيعة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r1.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi recounts that Mary fled with Joseph the carpenter after he learned she was accused of illicit pregnancy; Gabriel told him Jesus was from the Holy Spirit. Ibn Atiyya calls the story weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: قيل ليوسف وكانت سميت له أنها حملت من الزنى

QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya judges the story of Mary’s flight with Joseph the carpenter weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا كله ضعيف

QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r3.speaker: عكرمة
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r3.claim: Ikrima says Mary carried Jesus for eight months, prompting the claim that an eight-month infant cannot survive as a special sign of Jesus.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r3.anchor: وتظاهرت الروايات بأنها ولدته لثمانية أشهر. قاله عكرمة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r4.claim: Other reports say Mary delivered after nine months or six months; Qurtubi says Ibn Abbas’s account of immediate birth is sounder and more apparent.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r4.anchor: وقيل: ولدته لتسعة. وقيل: لستة. وما ذكرناه عن ابن عباس أصح وأظهر

QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the voice from beneath Mary was Gabriel, and Jesus did not speak until she brought him to her people.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r5.anchor: جبريل، ولم يتكلم عيسى حتى أتت به قومها

QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r6.speaker: علقمة والضحاك وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r6.claim: Alqama, al-Dahhak, and Qatada likewise identify the caller as Gabriel rather than the infant Jesus.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r6.anchor: علقمة والضحاك وقتادة ففي هذا لها آية وأمارة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r7.claim: The angel’s call was a sign to Mary that a supernatural event had a great divine purpose.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24/r7.anchor: ففي هذا لها آية وأمارة أن هذا من الأمور الخارقة للعادة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r1.claim: The phrase not to grieve explains the preceding call and means Mary should not grieve over giving birth.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r1.anchor: وأن» مفسرة بمعنى أي المعنى: فلا تحزني بولادتك

QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r2.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r2.claim: Hasan says the sariyya is Jesus, a noble and excellent man.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r2.anchor: يعني عيسى. والسري من الرجال العظيم الخصال السيد

QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r3.speaker: جمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r3.claim: Most commentators take the sariyya to be a stream near the palm; Ibn Abbas says God restored water to a river that had dried up.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r3.anchor: وقال الجمهور: أشار لها إلى الجدول الذي كان قريب جذع النخلة

QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says God caused water to flow again in a river that had dried up for Mary.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r4.anchor: كان ذلك نهرا قد انقطع ماؤه فأجراه الله تعالى لمريم

QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r5.claim: Sariyya can name a stream because water runs through it, as illustrated by cited poetry.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r5.anchor: والنهر يسمى سريا كأن الماء يسري فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r6.claim: Another view says Jesus called to Mary; this would be a miracle that reassured her, but Qurtubi prefers the stream interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r6.anchor: وقيل: ناداها عيسى، وكان ذلك معجزة وآية وتسكينا لقلبها والأول أظهر

QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas recited the phrase as an angel from beneath her; the explanation places Gabriel on lower ground.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:24-26/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس «فناداها ملك من تحتها

RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r1.speaker: زر
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r1.claim: The well-known reading is fanādāhā; Zirr and ʿAlqama read fa-khāṭabahā, “he addressed her.”

RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r2.speaker: نافع
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r2.claim: For min, Nāfiʿ reads the initial mīm with kasr, while the common reading has fatḥ; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ also read kasr.
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r2.anchor: وكسره وهو قراءة نافع وحمزة والكسائي وحفص

RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the caller as Jesus, as does Saʿīd ibn Jubayr.
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r3.anchor: أنه عيسى عليه السلام وهو قول الحسن وسعيد بن جبير

RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r4.speaker: جبريل
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r4.claim: Another view identifies the caller as Gabriel, who attended Mary like a midwife.
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r4.anchor: أنه جبريل عليه السلام وأنه كان كالقابلة للولد

RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r5.speaker: ابن عيينة
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r5.claim: A report from Ibn ʿUyayna distinguishes the readings: under kasr the caller is the angel, under fatḥ it is Jesus; ʿĀṣim is also cited for this view.
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r5.anchor: وهو مروي عن ابن عيينة وعاصم

RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r6.claim: Razi prefers Jesus: fatḥ suggests someone already known to be below her, namely the child, whereas kasr does not require Gabriel; the place is also unsuitable for an angel because it exposes her private parts.
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r6.anchor: بفتح الميم إنما يستعمل إذا كان قد علم قبل ذلك أن تحتها أحدا

RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r7.speaker: الحسن بن علي
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī argues that Mary could signal Jesus as her answer only if she knew he could speak.
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r7.anchor: دليل الحسن بن علي عليه السلام أن عيسى عليه السلام لو لم يكن كلمها

RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r8.claim: If Jesus called, God made him speak at birth to comfort Mary, remove her loneliness, and show the status Gabriel had promised; if Gabriel called, he was sent to remind her of earlier good news.
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r8.anchor: فالمعنى أنه تعالى أنطقه لها حين وضعته تطييبا لقلبها

RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r9.speaker: الكلبي
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r9.claim: If Gabriel is the caller, “from beneath her” may refer to a shared level and a local reference point, so one nearer it is above and one farther below, as al-Kalbī explains for the battle verse.
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r9.anchor: وفسر الكلبي قوله تعالى : { إذ جاءوكم من فوقكم

RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r10.speaker: عكرمة
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r10.claim: If the phrase marks elevation, ʿIkrima reports that Mary gave birth on a raised place; another report has Gabriel call from beneath the palm tree.
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r10.anchor: وعلى هذا الوجه روي عن عكرمة أنها كانت حين ولدت على مثل رابية

RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r11.claim: The wording does not establish whether Mary saw the caller.
RAZI-FULL:v21p174#2/r11.anchor: يحتمل أن تكون مريم قد رأته وأنها ما رأته وليس في اللفظ ما يدل

RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r1.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r1.claim: All commentators except al-Ḥasan and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd take sarī as a stream or channel, named for the water that flows in it; those two identify Jesus as a noble, eminent person.
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r1.anchor: اتفق المفسرون إلا الحسن وعبد الرحمن بن زيد أن السري هو النهر

RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r2.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan first interprets sarī as Jesus, a noble man, but a report says he later retracted after Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥumayrī corrected him to “stream.”

RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r3.claim: The stream reading is supported by a prophetic report identifying sarī as a channel and by the instruction to eat and drink.
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r3.anchor: أنه سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن السري فقال

RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r4.claim: Those who read Jesus argue a stream would be beside Mary, not below her, and invoke the parallel describing Jesus and his mother sheltered at a hill with a spring; Razi answers that “below” can mark relative nearness on level ground.
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r4.anchor: أن النهر لا يكون تحتها بل إلى جانبها

RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r5.claim: If sarī is water, one view says Gabriel struck the ground with his foot and a fresh stream appeared; another says flowing water was already there.
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r5.anchor: أن جبريل عليه السلام ضرب برجله فظهر ماء عذب

RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r6.claim: Razi prefers the newly created stream because “God has made” indicates a new event and its appearance is a miraculous honor for Mary.

RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Farrāʾ use sarī generally for a stream, while al-Akhfash restricts it to a small river.
RAZI-FULL:v21p175/r7.anchor: وهو قول أبي عبيدة والفراء أو النهر الصغير على ما هو قول الأخفش

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r102.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r102.speaker: Ṭ, Ṭs, Z
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r102.claim: The speaker calling to Mary may be Gabriel or Jesus; many favor Jesus because he speaks from below after birth.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r102.anchor: many consider it more likely that it is Jesus addressing her after he has been delivered

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r103.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r103.speaker: Ṭ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r103.claim: If Gabriel is speaking, “from below her” may mean “in front of her.”
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r103.anchor: may mean “in front of her” (Ṭ, Ṭs).

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r104.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r104.speaker: Ṭ, Z
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r104.claim: “From below her” may refer to the feminine palm trunk; alternatively Gabriel may call from the valley or mountain foot.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r104.anchor: from below the palm trunk (Ṭ, Z), which is also grammatically feminine

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r105.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r105.speaker: IK, Qu, Ṭs, Z
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r105.claim: Sariyyan may mean a noble or distinguished person and describe Jesus rather than a rivulet.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r105.anchor: some suggest that sariyyan, which can also be an adjective meaning “noble” or “distinguished,” may be a description of Jesus himself

NAHHAS:v3p12/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p12/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p12/r1.claim: Madinans, Kufans, and Basrans except al-Ḥasan, Abū ʿAmr al-Nakhaʿī, and ʿĀṣim read the first من تحتها; Abū ʿUbayd says it can refer to Gabriel or Jesus, while the fatḥa reading refers to Jesus alone.
NAHHAS:v3p12/r1.anchor: فزعم أبو عبيد أن من قرأ من تحتها جاز في قراءته أن يكون لجبرئيل

NAHHAS:v3p12/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p12/r2.speaker: أبو عبيد
NAHHAS:v3p12/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayd assigns the caller as Gabriel or Jesus in one reading and Jesus alone in the fatḥa reading.
NAHHAS:v3p12/r2.anchor: ومن قرأ من تحتها فهو لعيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم خاصة

NAHHAS:v3p12/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p12/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p12/r3.claim: Al-Naḥḥās says من is a noun and تحتها an adverb; this does not rule out Gabriel as speaker, as in the earlier passage.
NAHHAS:v3p12/r3.anchor: قال أبو جعفر من اسم و تحتها ظرف ولا يمتنع أن يكون معناه لجبرئيل

TAB-FULL:v15p501/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p501/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p501/r1.claim: The majority read min tahtiha with kasra; interpreters differ whether the caller is Gabriel in front of Mary or Jesus beneath her.
TAB-FULL:v15p501/r1.anchor: تأويله، فمن متأول منهم إذا قرأه {من تحتها} [البقرة: 25] كذلك، ومن متأول منهم أنه عيسى، وأنه ناداها من تحتها بعد ما ولدته.

TAB-FULL:v15p501/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p501/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p501/r2.claim: Some Kufan and Basran readers open both ta vowels, taking Jesus, the one beneath Mary, as the caller.
TAB-FULL:v15p501/r2.anchor: وقرأ ذلك بعض قراء أهل الكوفة والبصرة: (فناداها من تحتها) بفتح التاءين من تحت، بمعنى: فناداها الذي تحتها،

TAB-FULL:v15p501/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p501/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، عمرو بن ميمون، الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v15p501/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, Amr ibn Maymun, and al-Dahhak identify the caller as Gabriel; Qatada says the call came from beneath the palm.
TAB-FULL:v15p501/r3.anchor: ذكر من قال: الذي ناداها من تحتها الملك: حدثنا ابن حميد، قال: ثنا يحيى بن واضح،

TAB-FULL:v15p501/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p501/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v15p501/r4.claim: Al-Suddi likewise says Gabriel called from beneath her and told her not to grieve.
TAB-FULL:v15p501/r4.anchor: عن السدي، {فناداها} [مريم: 24] جبرائيل {من تحتها ألا تحزني} [مريم: 24]

TAB-FULL:v15p503/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p503/r1.speaker: مجاهد، الحسن، وهب بن منبه، سعيد بن جبير، ابن زيد، أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v15p503/r1.claim: These authorities identify the caller beneath Mary as Jesus; Sa'id ibn Jubayr points to her later gesture, while Ubayy says the caller was the child she carried.
TAB-FULL:v15p503/r1.anchor: ذكر من قال: ناداها عيسى صلى الله عليه وسلم: حدثنا محمد بن بشار، قال: ثنا أبو عاصم،

TAB-FULL:v15p503/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p503/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p503/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas instead says Gabriel called Mary and Jesus did not speak until she came to her people.
TAB-FULL:v15p503/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس {فناداها من تحتها} [مريم: 24] قال: ناداها جبرائيل ولم يتكلم عيسى حتى أتت قومها

TAB-FULL:v15p503/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p503/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p503/r3.claim: Al-Tabari prefers Jesus as the caller.
TAB-FULL:v15p503/r3.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وأولى القولين في ذلك عندنا قول من قال: الذي ناداها ابنها

TAB-FULL:v15p506/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r1.claim: Al-Tabari prefers Jesus as caller because he is the nearest antecedent in the narrative, following the account that Mary carried him away.
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r1.anchor: عيسى، وذلك أنه من كناية ذكره أقرب منه من ذكر جبرائيل، فرده على الذي هو أقرب إليه أولى من رده على الذي هو أبعد منه،

TAB-FULL:v15p506/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r2.claim: Mary's later pointing to Jesus implies she knew he could speak; the context would have stated Gabriel's promise and instruction if he were the speaker.
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r2.anchor: ولعلة أخرى، وهي قوله: {فأشارت إليه} [مريم: 29] ولم تشر إليه إن شاء الله إلا وقد علمت أنه ناطق في حاله تلك،

TAB-FULL:v15p506/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r3.claim: Both readings are sound: kasra points to Jesus as the one named, while fatha makes Jesus the grammatical subject of the call.
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r3.anchor: فبين أن كلتا القراءتين أعني {من تحتها} [البقرة: 25] بالكسر، «ومن تحتها» بالفتح صواب.

TAB-FULL:v15p506/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd portrays Mary asking how she can defend herself without husband or master; Jesus says he will speak for her.
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r4.anchor: قالت: وكيف لا أحزن وأنت معي، لا ذات زوج فأقول من زوج، ولا مملوكة فأقول من سيدي،

TAB-FULL:v15p506/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r5.claim: Al-Tabari notes that if Gabriel had spoken, the account should have stated that Jesus would speak and told Mary to point him out.
TAB-FULL:v15p506/r5.anchor: ولو كان ذلك قولا من جبرائيل، لكان خليقا أن يكون في ظاهر الخبر، مبينا أن عيسى سينطق ويحتج عنها للقوم،

TAB-FULL:v15p507/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p507/r1.speaker: البراء بن عازب
TAB-FULL:v15p507/r1.claim: Al-Bara ibn Azib glosses sariya as a small stream or channel.
TAB-FULL:v15p507/r1.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق، قال: سمعت البراء يقول في هذه الآية {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} [مريم: 24] قال: الجدول

TAB-FULL:v15p507/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p507/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p507/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas calls it a river associated with Jesus and describes it as the stream flowing beneath Mary at the birth.
TAB-FULL:v15p507/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} [مريم: 24] وهو نهر عيسى

TAB-FULL:v15p507/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p507/r3.speaker: عمرو بن ميمون
TAB-FULL:v15p507/r3.claim: Amr ibn Maymun calls it a river from which one drinks or a small stream.
TAB-FULL:v15p507/r3.anchor: عن عمرو بن ميمون الأودي، قال في هذه الآية: {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} [مريم: 24] قال: السري: نهر يشرب منه

TAB-FULL:v15p507/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p507/r4.speaker: مجاهد، ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v15p507/r4.claim: Mujahid says sariya is a river in Syriac; Ibn Jurayj says it is a river beside Mary.

TAB-FULL:v15p507/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p507/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v15p507/r5.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says sariya is a small river, called sariya in Nabataean.
TAB-FULL:v15p507/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} [مريم: 24] قال: هو الجدول، النهر الصغير،

TAB-FULL:v15p509/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r1.speaker: إبراهيم، الضحاك، قتادة، وهب بن منبه، السدي
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r1.claim: Ibrahim, al-Dahhak, and Qatada call sariya a small stream; Wahb says spring water, and al-Suddi says river.
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r1.anchor: حدثنا أبو كريب، قال: ثنا هشيم، عن مغيرة، عن إبراهيم، قال: النهر الصغير

TAB-FULL:v15p509/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r2.claim: Al-Hasan, reporting from Qatada, identifies sariya with Jesus himself.
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، عن الحسن، {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} [مريم: 24] والسري: عيسى نفسه

TAB-FULL:v15p509/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says sariya is Jesus, the most noble one, and argues a river would be beside Mary rather than beneath her.
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله {قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا} [مريم: 24] يعني نفسه، قال: وأي شيء أسرى منه،

TAB-FULL:v15p509/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r4.claim: Al-Tabari prefers the small stream: God supplied water for Mary to drink alongside the dates to eat, and the term is known in Arabic for a small river.
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r4.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وأولى القولين في ذلك عندي بالصواب قيل من قال: عنى به الجدول، وذلك أنه أعلمها ما قد أعطاها الله من الماء

TAB-FULL:v15p509/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r5.claim: Arabic usage and Labid's verse support sariya meaning a small river.
TAB-FULL:v15p509/r5.anchor: والسري معروف من كلام العرب أنه النهر الصغير، ومنه قول لبيد:

TAB-FULL:v15p510/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p510/r1.speaker: لبيد
TAB-FULL:v15p510/r1.claim: Labid's verse uses sariya for a stream crossed across its width.
TAB-FULL:v15p510/r1.anchor: فتوسطا عرض السري وصدعا … مسجورة متجاورا قلامها

TABATABAI:19:21-24/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:21-24/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:21-24/r7.claim: The one calling from beneath Mary is Jesus, since the phrase fits a newborn at his mother's delivery and nearby pronouns refer to him.
TABATABAI:19:21-24/r7.anchor: لعيسى عليه السلام لا للروح السابق الذكر

TABATABAI:19:21-24/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:21-24/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:21-24/r8.claim: The alternative says the spirit stood beneath a hill where Mary delivered, but the wording provides no evidence for that scenario.
TABATABAI:19:21-24/r8.anchor: وقيل الضمير للروح وأصلح كون الروح تحتها بأنها كانت حين الوضع في أكمة

TABATABAI:19:21-24/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:21-24/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:21-24/r9.claim: The sequence suggests Mary spoke her wish at or just after delivery and Jesus immediately comforted her; her fear of dishonor was especially grave because she was a chaste, defenseless virgin from a respected family.
TABATABAI:19:21-24/r9.anchor: فعقبها عليه السلام بقوله لا تحزني

TABATABAI:19:24-26/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:24-26/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:24-26/r1.claim: Sari means a stream, which fits the following command to eat and drink; the alternate meaning “noble, elevated person,” identified with Jesus, is not supported by context.

TABATABAI:19:40/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:40/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:40/r7.claim: Reports differ over whether Gabriel or Jesus caused a spring to appear by striking the ground; the report from al-Bāqir favors Jesus.
TABATABAI:19:40/r7.anchor: قيل ضرب جبرئيل برجله فظهر ماء عذب وقيل بل ضرب عيسى برجله فظهرت عين ماء تجري

TABATABAI:19:40/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:40/r8.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:19:40/r8.claim: The Prophet identifies the sariyy beneath Mary as a river; another report through Ibn ʿUmar says God made it flow for her to drink.
TABATABAI:19:40/r8.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في قوله { قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا } قال النهر

TABRISI:19:24/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:24/r2.speaker: أهل المدينة والكوفة غير أبي بكر وسهل
TABRISI:19:24/r2.claim: These readers use min tahtiha with a kasra under the m; the others use the open reading.
TABRISI:19:24/r2.anchor: وقرأ من تحتها بكسر الميم أهل المدينة والكوفة غير أبي بكر وسهل

TABRISI:19:24/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:24/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABRISI:19:24/r3.claim: Nasy is a negligible thing easily forgotten, such as a sandal or whip; other lexicographers call it the least significant thing.
TABRISI:19:24/r3.anchor: النسي هو الشيء الحقير ينسى نحو النعل والسوط

TABRISI:19:24/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:24/r4.speaker: الشنفرى
TABRISI:19:24/r4.claim: Al-Shanfara’s poem uses nasy for a small, overlooked object that is searched for on the ground.
TABRISI:19:24/r4.anchor: كأن لها في الأرض نسيا تقصه على أمها

TABRISI:19:24/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:24/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:19:24/r5.claim: The caller from beneath Mary may be Gabriel or Jesus; some insist it must be Jesus because Gabriel would call from above.
TABRISI:19:24/r5.anchor: وقال بعض أهل التأويل لا يكون إلا عيسى ع ولا يكون جبرائيل

TABRISI:19:24/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:24/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:24/r6.claim: The author favors Jesus as the caller because he would most directly remove Mary’s grief; beneath can mean below or near, not necessarily the lower direction.
TABRISI:19:24/r6.anchor: والأشبه أن يكون المنادي لها عيسى فإنه أشد إزالة لما خامر قلبها

TABRISI:19:24/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:24/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:24/r8.claim: Min tahtiha can mean from beneath or in front of her, by analogy with the stream described as beneath her; the wording may name Jesus generally after a narrower reference.
TABRISI:19:24/r8.anchor: ولم يكن النهر محاذيا لهذه الجهة ولكن المعنى جعله دونك

TABRISI:19:21-30/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:21-30/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:21-30/r5.claim: Sari means a flowing stream; jani means fruit picked or gathered.

TABRISI:19:25#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:25#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وسعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:19:25#2/r8.claim: The stream beneath Mary was restored by God so she could drink and cleanse herself after childbirth.
TABRISI:19:25#2/r8.anchor: قد جعل ربك تحت قدميك نهرا تشربين منه وتتطهرين من النفاس

TABRISI:19:25#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:25#2/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:19:25#2/r9.claim: One report says Jesus struck the ground with his foot, causing a spring to gush forth; other reports credit Gabriel or God directly.
TABRISI:19:25#2/r9.anchor: بل ضرب عيسى برجله فظهرت عين ماء تجري

THALABI:v6p211/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p211/r3.speaker: الحسن وأبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع وابن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي
THALABI:v6p211/r3.claim: These readers pronounce min taḥtihā with kasra and identify the caller as Gabriel calling from the mountain slope.
THALABI:v6p211/r3.anchor: قرأ الحسن وأبو جعفر وشيبة ونافع وابن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي: من تحتها بكسر الميم

THALABI:v6p211/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p211/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p211/r4.claim: The remaining readers pronounce min taḥtihā with fatḥa and identify the caller as Jesus emerging from Mary’s womb.
THALABI:v6p211/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون من تحتها بفتح الميم وهو عيسى لما خرج من بطنها ناداها

THALABI:v6p211/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p211/r5.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v6p211/r5.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the sariy as Jesus, a noble and elevated servant.
THALABI:v6p211/r5.anchor: قال الحسن: يعني عيسى كان والله عبدا سريا أي رفيعا

THALABI:v6p211/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p211/r6.speaker: سائر المفسرين
THALABI:v6p211/r6.claim: Most commentators interpret the sariy as a small river.
THALABI:v6p211/r6.anchor:
وقال سائر المفسرين:
هو النهر الصغير

THALABI:v6p211/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p211/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p211/r7.claim: “Beneath you” can mean that the river was placed under Mary’s command, flowing or stopping at her direction.
THALABI:v6p211/r7.anchor: إن الله تعالى جعل النهر تحت أمرها إن أمرته أن يجري جرى وإن أمرته بالإمساك أمسك

THALABI:v6p211/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p211/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p211/r8.claim: Gabriel—or, in another version, Jesus—struck the ground; a fresh spring appeared, and the dried palm revived, blossomed, fruited, and ripened.
THALABI:v6p211/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فضرب جبرئيل: ويقال عيسى: برجله الأرض فظهرت عين ماء عذب وجرى وحييت النخلة بعد يبسها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r1.claim: He says Gabriel heard Maryam's distress and called from below her, beneath the mound; al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and Qatada also identify Gabriel at the mountain's foot.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r1.anchor: سمع جبريل كلامها وعرف جزعها فناداها من تحتها أسفل منها تحت الأكمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r2.claim: They identify the caller as Jesus; Wahb, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, and Ibn Zayd share this view.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r3.claim: If Jesus called her, his speech serves to show her the sign in him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r3.anchor: أن يبين الله لها الآية في عيسى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r4.claim: He considers Jesus the more fitting caller because hearing him removes her loneliness and grief and answers possible accusations against her.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r4.anchor: أن يكون المنادي لها عيسى أشبه وأشد إزالة لما خامرها من الوحشة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r5.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r5.claim: He prefers the reading مِن تحتها with fatḥ on mīm, taking the general word as referring specifically to Jesus.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p224#2/r5.anchor: أبو علي: (وأن يكون المنادي لها عيسى أشبه وأشد إزالة لما خامرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r1.claim: Sari means a stream; he says its watercourse had dried up and God caused the water to flow for Maryam, as the majority of exegetes hold.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r1.anchor: ابن عباس: (يريد السري الجدول، وكان ساقيه للماء قبل ذلك، ثم انقطع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r2.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r2.claim: He also interprets sari as Jesus, saying Jesus was a noble man; after recognizing that Arabs call a river sari, he returned to the river interpretation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r2.anchor: الحسن أنه قال: (يعني عيسى عليه السلام، كان والله سريا من الرجال)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r3.claim: Linguists agree that sari means a river or stream; Labid's verse is cited as evidence.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r3.anchor: هذا القول. ولا خلاف بين أهل اللغة أن السري: النهر بمنزلة الجدول)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r4.claim: He explains under you as level with Mary's feet, consistent with the report that Gabriel struck the ground beneath her; another report says Jesus struck it and water emerged.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r4.anchor: الكلبي: (بحيال قدميك) (¬1). فجعل تحت هاهنا إسما للجهة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r5.speaker: أبو الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r5.claim: Alternatively, تحتك means below you in rank or position, not necessarily physically aligned with Maryam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r5.anchor: لهذه الجهة، ولكن المعنى جعله دونك، وقد يقال: فلان تحتنا أي: دوننا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r6.claim: Another interpretation makes the river subject to Mary's command, as Pharaoh's rivers were said to flow beneath him, meaning under his authority.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p225/r6.anchor: جعل النهر تحت أمرها إن أمرته أن يجري جرى

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:24-26/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:24-26/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:24-26/r1.claim: The stream was a flowing river below the hill; its water had stopped, so God sent water through it for Mary.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:24-26/r1.anchor: نهر ماء جار، وكان تحت الأكمة نهر قد انقطع الماء منه، فأرسل الله سبحانه الماء فيه لمريم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220/r8.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220/r8.claim: Qatāda says they used to report that the one calling Mary from beneath was the angel Gabriel.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220/r8.anchor: قوله: {فناداها من تحتها} [مريم: 24] سعيد، عن قتادة قال: كنا نحدث أنه الملك، يعني جبريل.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220#2/r1.claim: Yaḥyā heard one view that “from beneath her” means from below the ground; another says it refers to Jesus.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220#2/r1.anchor:
قال يحيى: سمعت من يقول: تحتها من الأرض.
وقال بعضهم: {تحتها} [مريم: 24] يعني عيسى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220#2/r2.speaker: البراء بن عازب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220#2/r2.claim: Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib says the sariya beneath Mary was a stream.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220#2/r2.anchor: حدثني يونس بن أبي إسحاق، عن أبيه، عن البراء بن عازب قال: هو الجدول.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220#2/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220#2/r8.claim: Sariyyan means a stream or river and is a Syriac word.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p220#2/r8.anchor: والسري هو الجدول، وهو النهر، وهو بالسريانية سريا.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:24/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
