KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:24/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:24/r1.claim: God consoles Mary by providing spring water to drink and fresh dates to eat.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:24/r1.anchor: onun için çıkardığı kaynak suyundan içecek, meyve vermesini sağladığı hurmadan da yiyecektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:24/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:24/r2.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:24/r2.claim: Shawkani says the phrase rendered as a spring beneath her could instead mean that Jesus was brought forth from her.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:24/r2.anchor: “Senden Îsâ’yı yaratıp çıkarmıştır” şeklinde çevirmek de mümkündür

SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r1.speaker: الأخوان
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r1.claim: The two Kufan readers, Nāfiʿ, and Ḥafṣ read min with kasra and taḥtihā in the genitive, making it a prepositional phrase and leaving nādā's subject implicit.
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r1.anchor: قوله: { من تحتهآ }: قرأ الأخوان ونافع وحفص بكسر ميم " من " ، وجر " تحتها " على الجار والمجرور.

SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r2.claim: On that reading the implicit caller may be Gabriel below Mary; Ibn ʿAbbās's explicit reading names an angel beneath her.
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r2.anchor: فالقراءة الأولى تقتضي أن يكون الفاعل في " نادى " مضمرا وفيه تأويلان، أحدهما: هو جبريل ومعنى كونه

SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās's reading makes the caller explicit as an angel beneath her.
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r3.anchor: ويدل على ذلك قراءة ابن عباس " فناداها ملك من تحتها

SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r4.claim: Alternatively, the implicit caller is Jesus, calling from beneath her skirt; the phrase can attach to the call or describe the caller's state, with the latter clearer.
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r4.anchor: وثاني التأويلين: أن الضمير لعيسى، لأي: فناداها المولود من تحت ذيلها.

SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r5.speaker: الباقون
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r5.claim: The other readers have fatḥa on min and accusative taḥtahā, construing min as a relative pronoun referring either to Gabriel or Jesus.
SAMIN-DURR:19:24/r5.anchor: والقراءة الثانية: تكون فيها " من " موصولة، والظرف صلتها، والمراد بالموصول: إما جبريل، وإما عيسى.

SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r1.claim: In allā taḥzanī, an may be explanatory after a verb of saying, with lā prohibitive and nūn deletion for the jussive; alternatively it is subjunctive with lā negative and deletion for the subjunctive.
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { ألا تحزني } يجوز في " أن " أن تكون مفسرة لتقدمها ما هو بمعنى القول، و " لا " على هذا ناهية

SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r2.claim: The syntactic position of an is accusative or genitive, the latter by an omitted preposition: nādāhā bi-kadhā.
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r2.anchor: ومحل " أن ": إما نصب أو جر لأنها على حذف حرف الجر، أي: فناداها بكذا.

SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r3.claim: The pronoun in taḥtahā can refer to Mary or the palm tree; Mary is preferred because it keeps the two pronouns aligned.
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r3.anchor: والضمير في " تحتها ": إما لمريم عليها السلام، وإما للنخلة، والأول أولى لتوافق الضميرين.

SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r4.claim: Sariyyan may be the first object and taḥtaki the second if jaʿala means make or render; if it means create, taḥtaki is syntactically extra.
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r4.anchor: قوله: " سريا " يجوز أن يكون مفعولا أول، و " تحتك " مفعول ثان لأنها بمعنى صير.

SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r5.claim: One meaning of sariyy is a man of elevated rank, derived from sarā yasrū; the verse refers to Jesus.
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r5.anchor: والسري فيه قولان، أحدهما: أنه الرجل المرتفع القدر، من سرو يسرو كشرف يشرف

SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r6.claim: The source notes irregular plurals for this meaning: sarāh and sarwāʾ, though asriyāʾ is the expected form.
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r6.anchor: ويجمع " سري " على " سراة " بفتح السين، وسرواء كظرفاء، وهما جمعان شاذان

SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r7.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r7.claim: Al-Rāghib derives sariyy from stripping a garment or removing a horse's saddle, as if the person had cast off his covering.
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: السري: من سروت الثوب، أي: نزعته، وسروت الجل عن الفرس، أي: نزعته. كأن السري سرى ثوبه، بخلاف المدثر والمتزمل. قاله الراغب.

SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r8.claim: Another meaning is a small stream, suiting the instruction to eat and drink; sarā yasrī refers to water flowing in it.
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r8.anchor: والثاني: أنه النهر الصغير، ويناسبه " فكلي واشربي " واشتقاقه من سرى يسري

SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r9.speaker: لبيد
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r9.claim: Labīd's verse uses al-sarī for a stream, describing passage across its breadth.
SAMIN-DURR:19:24#2/r9.anchor:
وأنشدوا للبيد:
3221- فتوسطا عرض السري فصدعا

ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r5.claim: With the reading min taḥtihā, the caller is Jesus beneath Mary; the more common reading is with kasra, while the other interpretation takes the caller to be an angel.
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r5.anchor:
ومن قرأ (من تحتها) عنى
عيسى عليه السلام.

ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r6.claim: The call by Jesus would make his sign manifest and assure Mary that God would make a sign for her in the palm tree.
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r6.anchor:
ويكون المعنى في مناداة عيسى لها أن يبين الله لها الآية
في عيسى،

ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r7.speaker: الحسن
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says sariyy means Jesus, a noble man; realizing that Arabs use sariyy for a river, he returned to that interpretation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r7.anchor:
روي عن الحسن أنه قال يعنى عيسى، وقال: كان والله سريا من
الرجال،

ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r8.claim: Arabic scholars agree that sariyy means a river like a small channel; Ibn Abbas gives the same explanation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r8.anchor: ولا اختلاف بين أهل اللغة أن السري النهر بمنزلة الجدول

ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r9.speaker: لبيد
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r9.claim: Labīd’s poem uses al-sarī for a river or stream; the witnessed word is al-sarī.
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r9.anchor:
قال لبيد:
فتوسطا عرض السري وصدعا. . . مسجورة

ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says sariyy is a river and cites a poem describing a dog drinking from it; the witnessed word is al-sarī.
ZAJJAJ:v3p324/r10.anchor:
وقال ابن عباس: السري النهر وأنشد.
سلم ترى الدالي منه أزورا.

ASAD-NOTES:19:23#n18/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:23#n18/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:23#n18/r1.claim: The phrase may mean the voice came from beneath Mary.

ASAD-NOTES:19:23#n18/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:23#n18/r2.speaker: Qatadah
ASAD-NOTES:19:23#n18/r2.claim: Qatadah, as quoted by Zamakhshari, takes the phrase to mean the voice came from beneath the palm tree.
ASAD-NOTES:19:23#n18/r2.anchor: interprets this as meaning "from beneath the palm-tree"

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The caller is the angel, and the phrase below her refers to the palm tree.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: these words were uttered by the angel

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Sarī refers to a small spring that God made flow for Mary.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Your Lord has made a stream to flow from below you.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Though deeply distressed, Mary complained only to God and did not act wrongly in frustration; this was her test, after which extraordinary divine mercy appeared.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Mary (sws) neither complained to anyone except God nor took a wrong step out of frustration.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p196#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p196#2/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p196#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Abu Bakr from Asim, and Ibn Amir open the vowels in من تحتها; Nafi, Hamza, al-Kisai, and Hafs break them.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p196#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وابن عامر: (من تحتها) بفتح الميم والتاء.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p196#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p196#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p196#2/r2.claim: Some exegetes say the caller must be Jesus, not Gabriel, since Gabriel would have called from above her.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p196#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعض أهل التأويل: لا يكون إلا عيسى، ولا يكون جبريل لأنه لو كان جبريل لناداها من فوقها.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p196#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p196#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p196#2/r3.claim: Al-Farisi allows Gabriel as caller: من تحتها can mean nearby or below her, not directly beneath; the following تحتك سريا supports that usage.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p196#2/r3.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يكون جبريل، وليس قوله من تحتها يراد به الجهة المحاذية للتمكن من تحته،

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p237/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p237/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p237/r3.claim: With fatḥa on mīm and tāʾ, man taḥtahā is the person below Mary, identified as Jesus; the locative phrase is an adverbial object for the place where the caller is.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p237/r3.anchor: لمن فتح أنه جعله اسم عيسى وفتح التاء لأنه ظرف مكاني متضمن لجثة

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p237/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p237/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p237/r4.claim: With kasra on mīm and tāʾ, min is a preposition governing the place below her, which is conceived as a container in which the action occurs.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p237/r4.anchor: لمن كسر الميم والتاء أنه جعلها حرفا خافضا للظرف لأنه اسم للموضوع

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p237/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p237/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p237/r5.claim: The caller is Gabriel; min can mark an origin, a partitive, or an emphatic addition.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p237/r5.anchor: والمراد بالنداء جبريل فأما مواقع من في الكلام فتقع ابتداء غاية

IBNMUJAHID:v1p407/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p407/r5.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p407/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim open mīm and tāʾ in min taḥtihā; Nāfiʿ, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ kasra both.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p407/r5.anchor: 8 واختلفوا فى فتح الميم والتاء وكسرهما من قوله ﴿ من تحتها ﴾ 24

QIRAAT-ER:19:24:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:24:3#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:24:3#1/r1.claim: Reading man as a relative pronoun instead of min as a preposition makes the one beneath Mary the caller, identifying the infant as subject.
QIRAAT-ER:19:24:3#1/r1.anchor: مَنْ (relative pronoun ""who/the one"") replaces مِنْ (preposition ""from""); تَحْتَهَا shifts to accusative

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r1.claim: Qatada says the one calling Mary from beneath was the angel, while Hasan says it was her son.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فناداها من تحتها ﴾ قال الملك وقال الحسن من تحتها هو ابنها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the stream beneath Mary as a small river; al-Bara ibn Azib gives the same explanation.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا ﴾ قال هو الجدول يعني النهر الصغير

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r3.speaker: البراء بن عازب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r3.claim: Al-Bara ibn Azib also identifies the sary as a small river.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p6#5/r3.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب في قوله تعالى ﴿ تحتك سريا ﴾ قال هو الجدول النهر الصغير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p235#3/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p235#3/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p235#3/r3.claim: Sarī can mean high in rank, or a small stream whose water flows through it; the two senses have different root endings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p235#3/r3.anchor: السري المرتفع القدر، يقال سرو يسرو، ويجمع على سراة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p235#3/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p235#3/r4.speaker: لبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p235#3/r4.claim: Labid’s verse uses sarā for a small watercourse or channel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p235#3/r4.anchor: وقال لبيد: فتوسطا عرض السرى فصدعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan like the previous one; Muqatil exempts the prostration verse, saying it was revealed in Medina after the migration to Abyssinia.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية كالسورة التي قبلها. وقال مقاتل: إلا آية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.claim: The surahs connect through astonishing stories: the earlier tells of the Cave, Moses and Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn; this one of John’s birth to an old man and barren woman and Jesus’ birth without a father.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.anchor: ومناسبتها لما قبلها أنه تعالى ضمن السورة قبلها قصصا عجبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r10.speaker: زر وعلقمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r10.claim: They are reported to read fa-khāṭabahā instead of fa-nādāhā; Abū Ḥayyān says it should be treated as explanation, not a canonical reading, since it differs from the agreed consonantal text.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r10.anchor: وقرأ زر وعلقمة فخاطبها مكان فناداها وينبغي أن يكون تفسيرا لا قراءة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r11.claim: The apparent caller is Jesus, whom God enabled to speak at birth; another view, from al-Ḥasan, says Gabriel stood on lower ground and called.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r11.anchor: والمنادى الظاهر أنه عيسى أي فولدته فأنطقه الله وناداها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads 'an angel called her from below.'
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r12.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس فناداها ملك من تحتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r13.speaker: نافع وحمزة والكسائي وحفص
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r13.claim: Among the listed readers, these use min as a preposition in min taḥtihā, 'from beneath her.'
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r13.anchor: نافع وحمزة والكسائي وحفص من حرف جر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r14.speaker: الابنان والأبوان وعاصم وزر ومجاهد والجحدري والحسن وابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r14.claim: They read man taḥtihā with fatḥa, meaning 'the one beneath her'; al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid identify him as the newborn Jesus.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r14.anchor: وقرأ الابنان والأبوان وعاصم وزر ومجاهد والجحدري والحسن وابن عباس في رواية عنهما من بفتح الميم بمعنى الذي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r15.claim: An is explanatory, introducing the message 'do not grieve.'
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r15.anchor: وأن حرف تفسير أي لا تحزني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r16.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r16.claim: Most interpret sariyyan as a stream; al-Ḥasan, Ibn Zayd, and Qatāda take it as an eminent man of standing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r16.anchor: والسري في قول الجمهور الجدول. وقال الحسن وابن زيد وقتادة عظيما من الرجال له شأن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r17.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r17.claim: Al-Ḥasan initially explains sariyyan as a noble, generous man, before Ḥumayd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān counters that he meant a stream.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p252/r17.anchor: وروي أن الحسن فسر الآية فقال: أجل لقد جعله الله سريا كريما فقال حميد بن عبد الرحمن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r1.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbās identifies sariyy as a stream of Jesus; another says it was the stream under Mary when she gave birth.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r1.anchor: أنه نهر عيسى، عن ابن عباس. وعنه أيضاً: الذي كان تحت مريم حين ولدته

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r2.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك وسعيد بن جبير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r2.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk call sariyy a river in Syriac, while Saʿīd ibn Jubayr gives the Coptic sense 'small stream'.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r2.anchor: وهو نهر بالسريانية عن مجاهد والضحاك، والجدول الصغير بالقبطية عن سعيد بن جبير

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r3.speaker: الحسن وغيره
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan and others take sariyy to mean Jesus himself; they argue that a river would be beside Mary, not underneath her.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r3.anchor: وقيل: هو عيسى نفسه، عن الحسن وغيره. قالوا: لو كان النهر لكان إمما يكون إلى جنبها، لا: من تحتها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r4.claim: The author favors a stream: the poetic evidence clearly supports that sense, and the wording 'under her' gives it a subtle, hidden quality.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r4.anchor: والشواهد من الشعر، صريحة في معنى النهر أو الجدول. وكون النهر من تحتها، فيه ملحظ الخفاء

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r5.claim: The surrounding account of Mary eating fresh dates and being told to eat and drink supports the stream interpretation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r5.anchor: مع سياق الآيات في الأكل من رطب النخلة، والشرب

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r6.claim: The author suggests the Qur'an's subtle choice is sharpened by sariyy occurring only once, unlike nahr and anhār, which occur five times.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p434/r6.anchor: الفرق الدقيق بين سرى، لم تأت غير مرة واحدة، والنهر والأنهار، وقد جاءا في القرآن الكريم خمس مرة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p432/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p432/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p432/r6.claim: In the question and answer, sariyy is glossed as a small river, with a line by Labīd ibn Rabīʿa cited as evidence.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p432/r6.anchor: قال: هو النهر الصغير. قال: وهل كانت العرب تعرف ذلك؟ قال: نعم، أما سمعت بقول لبيد بن ربيعة؟

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p432/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p432/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p432/r7.claim: A version attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās adds another poetic witness for sariyy as a stream.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p432/r7.anchor: وزاد في الأولى بالإسناد عن ابن عباس، قال: أما سمعت قول القائل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p601/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p601/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p601/r1.claim: The repeated فاء marks succession, with each event following according to its natural interval; it does not require every sequence to be instantaneous.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p601/r1.anchor: تكرر استخدام حرف الفاء وهي تفيد تعقيب كل شيء بحسبه أي تفيد تعقيب الأحداث التي وردت في السورة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p677/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p677/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p677/r1.claim: The author says سري means a master and its plural is سُراة, interpreting the phrase as God having made a master beneath Mary; a poetic line supports the plural.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p677/r1.anchor: كلمة السري وهي تعني (السيّد) وجمعها سُراة أي السادة

BURHAN:v1p219/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p219/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p219/r5.claim: The cited Qays kashkasha turns the feminine second-person kāf into shīn, so under you is pronounced rabbish taḥtish in the verse about Mary.
BURHAN:v1p219/r5.anchor: كشكشة قيس يجعلون كاف المؤنث شينا

ITQAN:v4p521/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p521/r1.speaker: النبي
ITQAN:v4p521/r1.claim: A weak-chain report from Ibn Umar says the sari beneath Maryam was a river God brought forth for her to drink.
ITQAN:v4p521/r1.anchor: أخرج الطبراني بسند ضعيف عن ابن عمر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

ITQAN:v2p400/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p400/r9.speaker: مجاهد
ITQAN:v2p400/r9.claim: Mujahid says “sari” means a river in Syriac.
ITQAN:v2p400/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ سريا ﴾ قال نهرا بالسريانية

ITQAN:v2p400/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p400/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ITQAN:v2p400/r10.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says “sari” is a word in the Nabataean language.

ITQAN:v2p360/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p360/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p360/r6.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ سريا ﴾ قال النهر الصغير

ITQAN:v2p319/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p319/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p319/r3.claim: The word sariyyan refers to Jesus.

ITQAN:v4p389/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p389/r2.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v4p389/r2.claim: The one who called to Mary from beneath her is identified as Jesus.

ITQAN:v4p389/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p389/r3.speaker: قيل
ITQAN:v4p389/r3.claim: An alternative identification of the one who called to Mary from beneath her is Gabriel.
ITQAN:v4p389/r3.anchor: ﴿ فناداها من تحتها ﴾ قيل عيسى وقيل جبريل

ITQAN:v2p397/r21.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p397/r21.speaker: أبو القاسم
ITQAN:v2p397/r21.claim: Abu al-Qasim says “from beneath her” means “from her belly” in Nabataean.
ITQAN:v2p397/r21.anchor: ﴿ فناداها من تحتها ﴾ أي بطنها بالنبطية

DAMGHANI:v1p258/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p258/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p258/r1.claim: Sariyy means a small river or stream, glossed as a small channel.
DAMGHANI:v1p258/r1.anchor: السري النهر الصغير قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p64/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p64/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p64/r1.claim: The author reads سريّ as master, with سُراة as its plural, and cites an Arabic line in which the plural appears.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p64/r1.anchor: فقد وردت كلمة السري وهي تعني

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p515/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p515/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p515/r1.claim: The word sariyy means a master or nobleman; its plural is surāt, supported by the cited line about nobles when the ignorant rule.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p515/r1.anchor: وهي تعني السيّد وجمعها سُراة أي السادة

NASHR:v2p318/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p318/r2.speaker: المدنيان وحمزة والكسائي وخلف وحفص وروح
NASHR:v2p318/r2.claim: For من تحتها, the two Medinese, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, Khalaf, Hafs, and Rawh read mīm with kasra and tāʾ in the genitive; the rest use fatḥa and accusative.
NASHR:v2p318/r2.anchor: وحفص وروح بكسر الميم وخفض التاء
